# Herdr selection list: `Blocked By` metadata line flickers endlessly on blocked items (WL-0MV8Q5X8U004KKAP)

**Headline:** The Herdr metadata panel has two live render states for a blocked item (async `Blocked By` lookup pending → line absent; resolved → line present), and `doRefresh()` clears the per-item blocker cache on *every* list refresh, so frequent refresh triggers (DB-change watch, auto-sync counter bumps, `wl next` re-sorts) re-flip the panel between the two states endlessly. Fix: make the resolved state survive refreshes and invalidate only when the item's dependency edges can actually change.

## Problem statement

In the Herdr work-item selection list, selecting a dependency-blocked item makes the metadata panel's `Blocked By` line appear for a moment, then disappear for a moment, then reappear — repeating endlessly. Selecting a blocked item is therefore visually noisy and leaves the "what is this blocked on?" answer (added by WL-0MV8EZRDJ001TDA8) unreliable at a glance.

## RCA (root cause analysis)

There are two distinct render states for the work-item preview, and the live loop flips between them on every refresh:

- **Path A — metadata panel, resolved:** `formatMetadataPanel(..., metaBlockedBy)` renders one `Blocked By` row per active blocker. `metaBlockedBy` is produced by `resolveMetaBlockers()` (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`), which resolves asynchronously via `fetchBlockersForItem()` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`; spawns `wl dep list <id> --json` plus one `wl show` per candidate blocker) and caches the result in an in-memory `blockerCache` keyed by item ID.
- **Path B — metadata panel, unresolved:** until the lookup lands (or after the cache is dropped), `resolveMetaBlockers()` returns `undefined`, `state.metaBlockedBy` is `null`, and the panel renders **without** the `Blocked By` rows. A follow-up `render()` is scheduled from the fetch's `.finally()`, so the line pops in ~one lookup latency later (~0.5–2 s for two spawned `wl` processes).

**Why it repeats endlessly:** `doRefresh()` calls `blockerCache.clear()` on **every** list refresh (`worklist.ts`, in the refresh path). Every cache clear re-introduces the unresolved frame for the full async lookup, then the `.finally(render())` flips it back. Refreshes fire far more often than the 30 s tick in a live workspace:

- the DB-change watch (`db-change.ts`) reacts within ~150 ms (debounce) to any `wl` state-counter bump — real agent writes, and *every successful auto-sync* (`src/commands/sync.ts` bumps the read-cache counter) — each feeding `requestWatchRefresh → doRefresh`;
- the auto-sync task itself runs `doRefresh(false)` unconditionally on its cadence;
- `wl next` re-sorts bump the counter when the dispatcher runs it (`src/commands/next.ts`).

So under sustained write/sync traffic the line alternates on/off continuously — the reported "for a moment… disappear for a moment… repeat endlessly". The design intent ("an unresolved item renders without rows and a follow-up render shows them") assumed a one-time transition per selection; invalidating the cache on every refresh breaks that assumption.

**Secondary inconsistency (the "other path" the report refers to):** only the list-mode metadata panel renders `Blocked By`. The **detail view** (`formatDetailContent`, the other work-item preview render path) builds its metadata table from `buildMetaRows()` without blocker rows, and the hover tooltip (`formatTooltipLines`) also omits them — so the two preview render paths have already diverged (one has the line, the other does not).

## Users

- **Producer / operator** browsing the Herdr selection list. Story: "When I select a blocked item, I want the `Blocked By` line to appear once and stay put until the data actually changes — not flash on and off."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Selecting a dependency-blocked item shows the `Blocked By` line stably: once resolved, no render frame drops the line on subsequent auto-refresh ticks, DB-change (watcher) refreshes, or auto-sync cycles; observed over ≥3 consecutive refresh cycles with the DB otherwise idle.
- [ ] List refreshes never blank the panel: a refresh reuses the last known blockers for the same selected item (or resolves from the freshly fetched payload) instead of re-running the async lookup and rendering an unresolved frame; there is at most one spawn of `wl dep list` (and enrichment) per item until its edges can actually change (selection change, or a refresh that changed the item's dependency set).
- [ ] The live loop is bounded and self-terminating: a blocked item under simulated refresh + counter/watch events ends in a stable frame set (exactly one unresolved→resolved transition per selection), never an oscillating pair.
- [ ] Unblocked items are unaffected: their metadata panel output is byte-for-byte unchanged; headings, list navigation, description preview, and `m`/`M` scroll clamping (including `metadataPanelContentHeight` with `metaBlockedBy`) behave as before.
- [ ] The two preview render paths are reconciled: the detail view either renders the same `Blocked By` rows as the list metadata panel, or this divergence is explicitly documented out of scope with a code comment — but the report's "two paths, one has the line, one does not" inconsistency must be resolved one way or the other.
- [ ] Fail-open behaviour is preserved: a failed `wl dep list`/`wl show` still yields no `Blocked By` rows and never breaks rendering or navigation.
- [ ] Regression tests cover: stable frames across repeated refreshes for a blocked selection; single-flight/no re-spawn for an unchanged selection; cache reuse semantics; and the detail-view parity decision.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list. It is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Display-only change**: the fix must not create or mutate dependency edges, and must not change list-data shape for non-panel consumers.
- **Render path must never block**: keep synchronous rendering; any resolution stays async but never causes a visual regression to an earlier frame.
- **Reuse existing helpers**: `isActiveBlocker()` (`packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts`) and `parseDepListBlockersOutput()` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`).
- **No extra `wl` spawns on refresh**: refresh must not re-run the per-item blocker lookup when nothing about that item's edges changed.
- **Scope**: primary fix is the selection-list metadata panel flicker. Detail-view/tooltip parity is secondary and decided within this item (fix or explicitly documented out of scope).

## Existing state

- `resolveMetaBlockers` + `blockerCache`/`blockerInFlight` (async, per-selection, cached by item ID, cleared in `doRefresh`) — introduced by WL-0MV8EZRDJ001TDA8.
- `formatMetadataPanel`/`buildMetadataPanelLines` render `Blocked By` rows from the `blockedBy` argument; `metadataPanelContentHeight` shares the same content so the scroll clamp matches the renderer (WL-0MV8EZRDJ001TDA8).
- The DB-change watch (`db-change.ts`) deliberately watches only the state-counter file to avoid the WAL/`-shm` self-sustaining loop (WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN); the counter is bumped by every `wl` write, successful `wl sync`, and `wl next` re-sort byproduct (`src/read-cache-cli.ts`, `src/commands/sync.ts`, `src/commands/next.ts`) — the refresh triggers that drive the flicker cadence.
- Loop-free refresh machinery (single-flight + trailing coalescing in `doRefresh`, debounced `requestWatchRefresh`, scheduler at `scheduler.ts`) is in place and must be preserved.

## Desired change

Make the `Blocked By` state transition idempotent and non-regressive per selection:

1. Keep the renderer's two states (with/without rows) but stop re-clearing the cache on unrelated refreshes — invalidate only when the selected item's dependency edges can have changed (new selection, or a refresh that changes the item), or resolve blockers from the fresh payload so the resolved state survives refresh atomically.
2. Cache the in-flight lookup itself so repeated refreshes never race/duplicate the spawn, and re-render from cache thereafter.
3. Decide and implement detail-view parity (render the same rows or document the divergence).

## Key Files:

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `resolveMetaBlockers`, `blockerCache.clear()` in `doRefresh`, render-loop wiring of `metaBlockedBy`; `formatDetailContent`/`formatTooltipLines` for parity.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `fetchBlockersForItem` (lookup + per-edge enrichment); consider promise-level memoisation.
- `packages/herdr/src/db-change.ts`, `src/read-cache-cli.ts`, `src/commands/sync.ts`, `src/commands/next.ts` — the refresh triggers whose counter bumps set the flicker cadence (context; not expected to change).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-blockers.test.ts` — regression tests.

## Related work

- WL-0MV8EZRDJ001TDA8 — "Show what an item is blocked on": parent feature that introduced the flickering async render path (regression source).
- WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN — "…DB-change watch" producer-rejection fix: the loop-free state-counter contract any fix must respect.
- WL-0MSGAEC5N006W5QA / WL-0MSGAEJQA005QG3W — read-cache + sync-heartbeat work that bumps the counter on sync (refresh frequency context).
- WL-0MSBVBNGH002RDP5 — prior "momentary collapse on refresh (flicker)" bug: the refresh path must stay atomic.
- WL-0MT9ZJF28004UJ28 — description-preview caching in the same metadata panel (precedent for cache-invalidation semantics).

### Related work (automated report)

- **WL-0MQP303A900780R0** – Escape key in Pi TUI work item detail view should navigate back to selection list (completed)
- **WL-0MT1JH1HN004JP1F** – T5: Metadata panel group info on heading (completed)
- **WL-0MQEJ2SLX009X17O** – Add risk and effort T-shirt size icons to Pi TUI work item selection list (completed)

Repository file matches: `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` (keyword overlap only).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the reported flicker is the list-mode metadata panel alternating between the unresolved and resolved `Blocked By` frames on repeated refreshes; the "two paths" wording also matches the detail view missing the line. Both readings are covered in the ACs.
- **Assumption:** refreshes in the reporter's environment were frequent enough (live workspace with agent writes / auto-sync / dispatcher `wl next`) to make the per-refresh blanking look continuous. The fix must be robust even under a fast refresh loop.
- **Risk — over-invalidation fix:** caching forever can show stale blockers after a real dependency change; the invalidation rule must distinguish "nothing changed" (reuse) from "item changed" (re-resolve).
- **Risk — spawn amplification:** the current code already spawns `wl dep list` + up to N× `wl show` per lookup; the fix must not add spawns to the refresh path.
- **Scope-creep risk:** detail-view/tooltip parity is tempting to expand; keep it to fix-or-document per AC5. Extra ideas should be tracked as separate work items, not scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required — the seed report plus repository investigation were sufficient to define the problem and the measurable acceptance criteria.

- Q (implicit): "Which code path renders the `Blocked By` line, and why does it flicker?" — Answer (investigation): two live states in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `resolveMetaBlockers()` returns `undefined` while the async `fetchBlockersForItem()` lookup is pending (line absent) and the cached array once it lands (line present); `doRefresh()` clears `blockerCache` on every refresh, so each refresh re-enters the absent state. Source: `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (`resolveMetaBlockers`, `blockerCache.clear()` in `doRefresh`) and `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` (`fetchBlockersForItem`).
- Q (implicit): "Do the two preview render paths differ?" — Answer (investigation): yes — list-mode `formatMetadataPanel` renders `Blocked By`; the detail view `formatDetailContent` (and the hover tooltip `formatTooltipLines`) build metadata from `buildMetaRows()` only and omit it. Source: `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`.
- Q (implicit): "What sets the flicker cadence?" — Answer (investigation + empirical check): the DB-change watch/react + auto-sync (successful `wl sync` bumps the read-cache state counter) + `wl next` re-sort byproduct bumps; verified with `wl list`/`wl show`/`wl dep list --json` that plain reads do not bump the counter. Source: `packages/herdr/src/db-change.ts`, `src/read-cache-cli.ts`, `src/commands/sync.ts`, `src/commands/next.ts`.

# Feature: Regression tests: concurrent dev/origin ref moves green

**Parent:** WL-0MV5MYBKJ0033P8U (Finish-gate live-repo guard trips on concurrent dev ref movement in multi-agent repos)
**Issue type:** task (tests — test-first slice of the plan)

## Summary

Add hermetic regression tests at all three consumer levels (helper `diff_snapshots`/`fingerprint`, inner per-test guard, outer `guarded_run_all`) proving that concurrent movement of `refs/heads/dev`, `refs/remotes/origin/dev` and arbitrary `refs/remotes/origin/*` cannot fail the live-repo guard, while genuine mutations (fixture-branch creation, config rewrite, working-tree change) still do. These tests are the red half of a test-first vertical slice: they fail against the current code and go green once the F2 implementation item lands.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — Helper level: `diff_snapshots` reports `changed == false` when only `refs/heads/dev` moved (working tree and non-excluded config unchanged); `fingerprint()` agrees.
- [ ] AC2 — Helper level: `diff_snapshots` reports `changed == false` when only `refs/remotes/origin/dev` or an arbitrary `refs/remotes/origin/*` ref moved; `fingerprint()` agrees.
- [ ] AC3 — Helper level: a new non-excluded branch (fixture branch, e.g. `feature-x`), a removed/moved non-excluded ref, a local-config rewrite, and a working-tree change each still report `changed == true`.
- [ ] AC4 — Inner per-test guard (pytest subprocess on a `tmp_path` hermetic sandbox): a test that advances `refs/heads/dev` and `refs/remotes/origin/dev` mid-run passes the session clean; a test that creates a new non-excluded branch mid-run fails and names the test.
- [ ] AC5 — Outer `guarded_run_all`: mid-run `refs/heads/dev` + `refs/remotes/origin/dev` movement yields a clean run (no `live_repo_mutation`); a genuine new-branch mutation still fails the run.
- [ ] AC6 — Tests live in `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py`, `tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py` and `skill/test/tests/test_guarded_run_all.py`; the full project test suite (pytest + node, as declared by the test skill) passes once the F2 implementation lands.

## Target outcome

The finish-gate and per-test guards never fail solely because sibling agents advanced `dev` or fetched/pushed to `origin` during the ~17-minute suite run.

## Definition of done (pass/fail)

- Red: the new tests fail against the untouched `git_sandbox.py` (proving they exercise the gap). Green: they pass with the F2 helper change.
- All existing guard tests remain green (no exclusion regression).

## Minimal Implementation

- Helper tests (extend `TestAgentWorktreeChurn`/`TestOwnershipBasedExclusion`-style classes in `test_git_sandbox.py`): create a hermetic repo + remote via existing `git_sandbox` factories under `tmp_path`; snapshot before/after a plumbing move (`git update-ref`) of `refs/heads/dev`, `refs/remotes/origin/dev`, and an arbitrary `origin/*` ref; assert `changed == false` and equal fingerprints. Add adversary cases (new branch, config rewrite, working-tree change) asserting `changed == true`.
- Inner-guard tests (`tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py`): a conftest scenario whose test body advances `dev`/`origin/dev`; assert clean session; a sibling scenario creating a non-excluded branch asserts failure naming the test.
- Outer-guard tests (`skill/test/tests/test_guarded_run_all.py`): drive `guarded_run_all` with a command that moves `dev`/`origin/dev` mid-run; assert no `live_repo_mutation`; adversary case asserts failure.
- No production code change in this item (TDD red).

## Constraints

- Tests use the hermetic `git_sandbox` factories under `tmp_path` — never the live checkout.
- No `wl-*` name patterns in tests (the incident's fixture branches must remain detectable).
- Deterministic: ref movement via plumbing only, no timing dependence.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py`
- `tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py`
- `skill/test/tests/test_guarded_run_all.py`

- None (the F2 implementation item depends on this one).

- Red regression tests at all three levels plus the deterministic harness.

# Feature: Exclude dev + remote-tracking refs from guard diff

**Parent:** WL-0MV5MYBKJ0033P8U (Finish-gate live-repo guard trips on concurrent dev ref movement in multi-agent repos)
**Issue type:** feature (implementation slice)

## Summary

Because both consumers (F4 outer `run_tests.py:guarded_run_all`, F5 inner `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py`) share the helper, neither needs a code change and they cannot drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — `diff_snapshots` and `fingerprint` both report no change when only `refs/heads/dev` and/or `refs/remotes/origin/*` refs moved (movement or churn inside those namespaces is invisible).
- [ ] AC2 — Every other ref addition/removal/movement (e.g. fixture-branch creation like the incident's `feature-x` / `wl-*-test`), every local-config rewrite outside excluded branches, and every working-tree change still reports `changed == true` and fails the guard.
- [ ] AC3 — Existing exclusions are behaviour-preserving: `refs/worklog/*`, agent-worktree branch refs plus their `branch.<name>.*` config, and main-checkout anchoring all behave as before (existing regression tests stay green).
- [ ] AC4 — Helper-only: no consumer code change in `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` or `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py`; the F1 guard-level regression tests (inner + outer) pass via the shared helper.
- [ ] AC5 — Exclusion is expressed as ref-namespace constants (`refs/remotes/origin/` prefix, `refs/heads/dev` exact) — never a `wl-*` name pattern; snapshots stay read-only plumbing; the per-test `fingerprint` stays cheap (no `status` scan).
- [ ] AC6 — The full project test suite (pytest + node, as declared by the test skill) passes with the change.

## Target outcome

`implement.py finish` and `/skill:test` stay green on a shared multi-agent host while siblings move `dev`/`origin/*`; genuine in-place checkout mutation (the SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX `GIT_DIR`-leak class) still fails the gate.

## Definition of done (pass/fail)

- F1 helper + guard tests pass.
- Adversary tests still fail on genuine mutations.
- Full suite green.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add module constants (e.g. `CONCURRENCY_EXCLUDED_REF_NAMESPACES = ("refs/remotes/origin/",)` and `CONCURRENCY_EXCLUDED_REF_EXACT = "refs/heads/dev"`) plus one shared predicate `_is_concurrency_excluded_ref(ref)`.
- Apply the predicate to the ref filter in `diff_snapshots` (alongside the existing `excluded` set) and to the ref tuple in `fingerprint`. Keep raw refs in the snapshot for diagnostics/`describe_diff`.
- Verify no `branch.dev.*` config exclusion is required (dev-tracking config is static and not churned by a ref fast-forward); add it only if a guard test demonstrates churn.
- Run F1: helper + guard tests flip red → green.

## Constraints

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` stays stdlib-only and loadable by file location (no `sys.path` mutation).
- Exclusion derived from git plumbing/ref-namespace constants, never a `wl-*` name pattern.
- The fix must not silently disable detection of the SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX leak class (AC2; config + working-tree + non-excluded ref surfaces still fire).

# Intake Brief — Restore `needsProducerReview` flag and producer-review icon in herdr selection list (WL-0MVAMS4RO000H3B0)

## Problem Statement

The `needsProducerReview` flag — the mechanism that marks a work item as awaiting Producer sign-off and drives the release gate — was removed from the database, CLI/API and herdr UI by WL-0MV85WFYU0071YQ9 + WL-0MV85WGIT004PHRC (children of epic WL-0MV82CHGQ000HAZZ), along with the producer-review icon ❌/✅ that used to appear in the herdr selection-list row prefix. The operator states this removal **should never have been created and implemented** — it was a misunderstanding somewhere along the line. The visible symptom was reported as a bug: *"The icon indicating the producer review status is no longer visible in the selection list in herdr."* The producer hold was re-homed onto the `assignee` field (`wl update <id> --assignee Map`), which is only surfaced through review-queue ordering — no icon, no at-a-glance signal, and no flag on the work item. This item restores the flag and its selection-list icon to the pre-removal behaviour, and an RCA child (WL-0MVAOYBZM0065AEN) traces how the wrongful removal item came to be created.

## Users

- **Producer / operator** scanning the herdr selection list to see which items await their review.
  - *As the producer, I want the list to show which items are awaiting my review (❌) and which have been reviewed (✅) at a glance, so I don't have to open every item or memorise assignee quirks.*
- **Downstream consumers of the flag** (release gate, audit runner, heartbeat, downtime dispatcher).
  - *As the release pipeline, I want `needsProducerReview` to gate the ship again, so unreviewed work cannot be released while the operator still expects that guarantee.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **DB restored:** a new migration re-adds the `needsProducerReview` column (kept idempotent; the shipped `20261015-drop-…` migration is neutralised as a metadata-sentinel no-op, mirroring how `20260210-add-…` was preserved); the field is back on `WorkItem`/query/input types, `VALID_FIELDS`, JSONL transport and both persistent-store schemas/row mappings, pinned by the restored migration/round-trip tests.
2. **CLI/API restored:** `wl reviewed` returns (with help entry + completion); `--needs-producer-review` is accepted by `wl create`/`wl update` and as a filter on `wl list`/`wl search`/`wl next`; the `api.ts` query param and `cli-types` surface are restored. Verified by restoring `tests/cli/reviewed.test.ts` and `tests/api-needs-producer-review-filter.test.ts`-style coverage.
3. **Selection-list icon visible again:** `getIconPrefixParts` in `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` renders the producer-review column (❌ `[REVIEW]` when true, ✅ `[OK]` when false, for all stages; empty when unset) exactly as at `e0f04202^`; `noIcons`/`WL_NO_ICONS` fallbacks work; a regression test asserts a flag-true item's list row contains the icon and a flag-false item's row shows the "done" state.
4. **herdr wiring restored:** the 6-bucket `in_review` grouping predicate returns (bucket 1 = `needsProducerReview === true`); fetcher/downtime-worker `select*`/`classifyItemForDispatch` exclude flag-true items from auto-dispatch again; `index.ts`, pane-lifecycle, pane-close*, stalled-work, settings and `worklist.ts` carry/use the flag; the metadata panel row and help-screen icon legend are restored and the legend drift guard passes.
5. **Theme/interview/shortcuts restored:** `src/theme.ts` producer-review icon helpers return; `src/commands/interview.ts` flag explain/clear flow returns; `src/commands/grouping.ts` + `helpers.ts` stop branching on the assignee for review semantics; the `r p` shortcut (shortcuts.json) acts on `needsProducerReview` again.
6. **Release/dispatch semantics restored (cross-repo, tracked as SA items):** `skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js` blocks release on `needsProducerReview === true` and the audit runner (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`) sets the flag on 'yes' verdicts — implemented via SorraAgents work items, not edited from this repo.
7. **Docs updated:** `docs/icons-design.md` (§3b restored with the icon column), `CLI.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` describe the flag again; the interview skill's `wl reviewed` handoff reference in the shared contract becomes valid again once the command is restored.
8. **RCA delivered:** the RCA child WL-0MVAOYBZM0065AEN reaches a terminal stage with a written root-cause chain and 3–5 concrete process recommendations.
9. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** — managed by the ship skill's release pipeline. No CI/CD pipeline tests included.

## Constraints

- **Restore, don't redesign:** behaviour must match the pre-removal state (`e0f04202^` / `d18ea50d^`); do not invent a new icon scheme or flag semantics.
- **Migration history preserved:** never rewrite a shipped migration; add a new add-column migration and neutralise the shipped drop-migration (the established `20260210-add`/metadata-sentinel pattern).
- **Repo boundary:** `skill/` (SorraAgents) and `.pi/` files are not edited from this repo except the in-repo `.pi/skills/heartbeat` + `skill/pane-triage`-adjacent changes already made there; SA-side restore is tracked as SA work items linked from here.
- **Do not regress the legitimate audit-tier fix:** the status-neutral assignee-CAS claim and `--if-assignee` (WL-0MV7W77AY005MGBL fix within the epic) stay unless the RCA recommends otherwise — the flag's return must not reintroduce the `in-progress`/`in_review` hybrid claim bug.
- **UK English, Markdown descriptions, wl is source of truth**, push only to `dev`, build → test → commit order.
- **Sequencing:** the operator directed "restore … and then RCA" — the restore is the urgent (critical) deliverable; the RCA child follows/parallel and must not block the restore.

## Existing State

- Column dropped (`20261015-drop-needsProducerReview`); `wl reviewed` deleted (src/commands/reviewed.ts removed) and unregistered from CLI/help/completion; `--needs-producer-review` gone from create/update and list/search/next; api.ts param and cli-types removed; JSONL/type surface removed.
- Producer-review icon helpers, legend entries and the icon-prefix column removed from `packages/shared/src/icons.ts`; `src/theme.ts` helpers removed; `in_review` grouping collapsed to 5 buckets with bucket 1 = non-empty assignee (`inReviewBucket` in `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`).

# RCA: how WL-0MV85WGIT004PHRC (Remove needsProducerReview from herdr, theme and interview) came to be created and implemented

## Goal

Investigate the process/pipeline that created and implemented WL-0MV85WGIT004PHRC — and its parent epic WL-0MV82CHGQ000HAZZ (13 children) — which removed the `needsProducerReview` flag and its selection-list icon. The operator states this work should never have been created: it was a misunderstanding somewhere along the line. The RCA must produce a written root-cause analysis and concrete, adoptable process controls so a wrongful removal of this kind cannot recur.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A single written RCA report is appended to this work item's description (or a clearly linked comment), covering the five trace points: (a) decision trail from WL-0MV7W77AY005MGBL through the epic's 'Option A' intake; (b) whether interview questions were answered by the producer or auto-resolved by agents (the epic Appendix records no interactive interview — 'herdr-dispatched session; seed context was exhaustive' — and Q2/Q3 remain open); (c) which agent/automation created the epic and children, when, and on what evidence (wl/git records cited); (d) why an item removing a core, approved producer-review feature advanced through intake/plan/implement/in_review without producer approval; (e) process controls that would have prevented it.
2. The report contains an explicit root-cause chain — proximate cause(s) feeding systemic cause(s) — not just a narrative.
3. The report ends with 3–5 concrete process recommendations, each stating the specific control, where it applies (skill/workflow/worklog rule), and its observable success signal.
4. Every claim is evidence-linked: work-item ids (WL-0MV85WGIT004PHRC, WL-0MV82CHGQ000HAZZ, WL-0MV7W77AY005MGBL, WL-0MVAOYBZM0065AEN, epic children), commit hashes (e0f04202, d18ea50d), or wl/git command output quoted inline.
5. The report is reviewed and accepted by the producer (a producer comment confirming the findings/owners), completing the investigation as a terminal deliverable.
6. All related documentation discovered during the RCA is referenced (e.g. docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md, the shared interview contract's `wl reviewed` handoff reference).
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (RCA is investigation-only; no code change expected, so this is satisfied trivially unless the RCA itself corrects a doc).

## Constraints

- Investigation only: the RCA does **not** implement the restore — that is the parent WL-0MVAMS4RO000H3B0 delivered in parallel.
- Do not fabricate findings: if a trace point cannot be determined from records, state it explicitly as an evidence gap rather than guessing.
- UK English; Markdown; wl is the source of truth.

## Existing State / Evidence Trail

- WL-0MV85WGIT004PHRC (completed, in_review) — "Remove needsProducerReview from herdr, theme and interview"; commit d18ea50d.
- WL-0MV85WFYU0071YQ9 (completed, in_review) — "Remove needsProducerReview from the worklog core"; commit e0f04202.
- WL-0MV82CHGQ000HAZZ (completed epic, in_review) — "Option A … remove needsProducerReview"; 13 children; appendices record Q1 accepted (assignee sync), Q2 (producer-hold identity) and Q3 (dependency direction) left OPEN; source note: "No interactive interview conducted — herdr-dispatched session; seed context was exhaustive."
- WL-0MV7W77AY005MGBL (open) — root-cause bug the epic set out to fix; the epic holds depends-on to it.
- WL-0MVAOYBZM0065AEN — this item (discovered-from:WL-0MVAMS4RO000H3B0).
- Relevant code/docs: `packages/herdr/src/producer-hold.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`, `packages/shared/src/icons.ts`, `docs/icons-design.md` §3b, and the shared interview contract's `wl reviewed` handoff (command removed by the removal work).

## Deliverables

- Written RCA report (report body appended to this work item).
- Root-cause chain + 3–5 process recommendations with owners.
- Producer review/acceptance of the findings.

## Related work

- WL-0MVAMS4RO000H3B0 — parent (restore item this RCA was discovered from).
- WL-0MV85WGIT004PHRC / WL-0MV85WFYU0071YQ9 / WL-0MV82CHGQ000HAZZ — the subject of the RCA.
- WL-0MV7W77AY005MGBL — root-cause bug that motivated the epic.


---

## RCA report (deliverable)

Full report: `docs/dev/rca-wrongful-needsproducerreview-removal.md` (committed with this item).

**Headline:** WL-0MV85WGIT004PHRC (and sibling WL-0MV85WFYU0071YQ9) were wrongful removals created inside epic WL-0MV82CHGQ000HAZZ. The producer approved the epic's **fix mechanism** (status-neutral assignee CAS claim, bug WL-0MV7W77AY005MGBL Q1 = Option A) but **never approved removing the `needsProducerReview` feature** — no producer comment approving the flag/`wl reviewed`/icon removal exists in any item or appendix. The removal rode along as unrequested epic scope, advanced through an autonomous herdr-dispatched lifecycle (intake "seed context exhaustive", no interactive interview; Appendix Q2/Q3 left OPEN) through plan → implement → in_review, with every implementation leg overriding the 11-orphaned-stash hygiene warning and the final parent advancement being fully automated.

**Root-cause chain (proximate → systemic):**
1. Scope conflation — a legitimate claim fix bundled with an unapproved destructive removal in one epic.
2. No destructive-change approval gate — nothing requires producer sign-off before removal ACs advance.
3. Open producer questions did not block stage advancement (Q2 replacement semantics, Q3 dependency direction unanswered).
4. Option framing asked "which fix mechanism?" not "may we delete the producer-review feature?" — the deletion was buried in child descriptions.
5. Automated full-loop autonomy — intake→plan→implement→in_review with no human checkpoint.
6. Self-cleaning removal — the same commits deleted the feature's tests and docs, so nothing failed until the operator saw the TUI.

**Recommendations (3–5 process controls):**
1. Mandatory producer-approval AC for destructive removals; block advancement past `plan_complete` without evidence (intake/plan/tree_coverage/implement gate).
2. Unresolved producer OPEN QUESTIONS block `plan_complete`/`in_review` (shared coverage gate + parent advancement).
3. Separate "fix mechanism" from "feature removal" in epic option framing — every deletion delta gets its own producer answer in the Appendix.
4. Human checkpoint before automated parent advancement for removal-scope epics (parent phase refuses without producer confirmation; names removed surfaces).
5. Repo guard against self-cleaning removals: flag commits that delete protection tests AND touch the source module in the same change (pre-push/CI), aligned with the existing blame-guard test.

# Refresh selection list on focus

## Problem statement

When the worklog selection list regains focus — either its tab returns to the foreground (hidden → visible) or the list pane regains keyboard focus inside an already‑visible tab — the user expects the view to refresh immediately. Tab‑level refresh already ships (WL‑0MSBVS4AS006ZQEZ, WL‑0MSIG3IO7009RL03), but pane‑level (keyboard) focus inside a visible tab depends entirely on a `pane_focused` event stream that repeatedly closes (`stream_closed`), leaving the list stale until the next 30 s tick.

## Users

- **Herdr users with multi‑pane tabs** — the worklog list shares a tab with editor/agent panes; switching keyboard focus back to the list (click or focus chord) should show current data instantly, not up to 30 s later.
- **Herdr users with several tabs** — returning to a hidden tab containing the worklist expects an immediate refresh (already shipped; must not regress).

User stories:
- _As a herdr user in a split view, I want the worklist to refresh the moment I focus its pane, so I don't have to wait for the next refresh tick to see new work items._
- _As a user returning to a previously hidden tab, I want the list to refresh immediately and the paused indicator to clear without waiting for the next tick._

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Tab hidden → visible refresh retained:** when a hidden tab containing the worklist regains focus, the list re‑fetches immediately (outside the regular `refreshIntervalMs` tick) and the `[paused — hidden]` indicator clears — existing behaviour, regression‑tested.
2. **Pane‑level focus refresh:** when the worklog pane regains keyboard focus within an already‑visible tab (i.e. `pane_focused` for the current pane, `focused: true`), the list refreshes immediately.
3. **Event‑stream health:** the `events.subscribe` stream stays healthy over time — the client sends whatever keepalive/heartbeat (or equivalent) the herdr server expects, so streams no longer close into a ~10 s reconnect loop; a closed/errored stream reconnects promptly (backoff retained) and `pane_focused` events resume delivering refresh‑on‑focus.
4. **Diagnosis recorded:** the root cause of the repeated `stream_closed` completions is identified with log evidence; if the root cause is client‑side the fix lands in `events.ts` with no changes to the external herdr app/framework, and if it is server‑side the finding is documented and a blocker work item is raised.
5. **Pause‑when‑hidden preserved:** while hidden, refresh/sync ticks still spawn zero `wl` processes (WL‑0MSB1N0HB0007N6N); the zero‑spawn‑when‑idle guarantee is not weakened.
6. **Testing:** new unit tests cover the keepalive/reconnect resilience and the pane‑focus refresh path; the full `packages/herdr` test suite passes.
7. **Documentation:** all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments (`events.ts`, `worklist.ts`), README, and any relevant docs/wiki entries.
8. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **No changes to the external herdr app/framework** (the herdr CLI/server is the calling framework; its protocol and `stream_closed` semantics are treated as a given, though behaviour may be observed and documented).
- Must not regress the zero‑`wl`‑spawn‑when‑hidden behaviour (WL‑0MSB1N0HB0007N6N) or the tab‑focus visibility gating (WL‑0MSJNJPRM009RM35 / WL‑0MSKUAT5D00443GA).
- Keep changes surgical and client‑side: `packages/herdr/src/{events,worklist}.ts` (+ tests).
- **Scope note (approved):** no new pane‑level polling fallback. The approved scope from WL‑0MSKUAT5D00443GA ("no pane‑focus fallback") stands; pane‑level refresh is delivered by making the event path reliable, and the tab‑level `resume-poll` remains the events‑unavailable fallback. Revisit only if diagnosis shows events cannot be made reliable client‑side.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/events.ts` — `HerdrEventSubscriber` subscribes once to `pane.focused`, `pane.agent_detected`, `pane.closed`, `pane.exited` (+ per‑pane `pane.agent_status_changed`) over a Unix‑socket JSON‑RPC stream. It reconnects with exponential backoff (`RECONNECT_BASE_DELAY_MS = 500`, cap `MAX_RECONNECT_DELAY_MS = 10_000`). **It sends nothing after subscribing — no keepalive/heartbeat/ping.**
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `onPaneFocused` handler: for the current pane (`HERDR_PANE_ID`), `focused: false` → hidden/paused; otherwise → `paneGate.setVisibleFromEvent(true)`, clear paused, `doRefresh(true)`, `runHydrator()`. The `resume-poll` scheduler task is the events‑unavailable tab‑level fallback (runs only while hidden).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-visibility.test.ts` — covers tab hidden→visible via resume‑poll AND the `pane_focused` event path (WL‑0MSHB7DHO004RHBJ F3).
- `packages/herdr/src/events.test.ts` — covers subscription shape, dispatch, reconnect‑with‑backoff, close/cleanup. No keepalive coverage.

**Diagnostic evidence (2026‑10‑16):** `~/.config/herdr/herdr-server.log` shows `events.subscribe` requests completing with `outcome="stream_closed"` and, for one pane at 07:15–07:17, reconnecting on a ~10 s cadence (`sub-100`…`sub-115`, matching `MAX_RECONNECT_DELAY_MS`). `herdr-client.log` shows `client terminal unavailable; detaching err=I/O error (os error 5)` entries. Working hypothesis: the server closes idle subscription streams and the client — which sends no keepalives — re‑enters the backoff loop; or the connection drops for an environmental reason (terminal detach). Confirmation is part of implementation (AC4).

## Desired change

1. **Diagnose** the `stream_closed` reconnect loop (server log correlation, protocol expectations, whether a keepalive/ping is required) and record findings.
2. **events.ts:** add client‑side resilience so the subscription stream stays healthy — e.g. an application‑level keepalive/ping with server‑accepted framing, prompt re‑subscribe on stream close (without unbounded backoff growth on routine stream closes), and preservation of the `pane_focused` → refresh wiring.
3. **worklist.ts:** verify (and where needed harden) the pane‑focus refresh path (`onPaneFocused` → `doRefresh(true)`) and keep the tab‑level `resume-poll` as the fail‑open fallback; do not add a pane‑level poll.
4. Add/extend tests (events + worklist‑visibility) and document the mechanism and any limitation.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/events.ts` — keepalive/heartbeat or resilient re‑subscribe; fix the ~10 s reconnect loop (AC3/AC4).
- `packages/herdr/src/events.test.ts` — tests for keepalive + reconnect resilience (AC6).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — verify/harden `onPaneFocused` pane‑focus refresh wiring (AC2).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-visibility.test.ts` — regression + pane‑focus refresh tests (AC1/AC2/AC6).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` (or docs) — document the keepalive mechanism and any residual limitation (AC7).

## Related work

- **WL‑0MSBVS4AS006ZQEZ** — Herdr selection list refreshes immediately when its tab regains focus (completed): the tab hidden→visible immediate refresh.
- **WL‑0MSHB7DHO004RHBJ** / **WL‑0MSIG3IO7009RL03** — Subscribe to herdr window events; pane_focused event path (completed): the event‑driven visibility + refresh wiring this item must keep healthy.
- **WL‑0MSJNJPRM009RM35** / **WL‑0MSKUAT5D00443GA** — Tab‑focus visibility gating; approved "no pane‑focus fallback" scope (completed).
- **WL‑0MSB1N0HB0007N6N** — Pause‑when‑hidden / zero‑wl‑when‑hidden (completed): constraint that must not regress.
- **WL‑0MTV67MZU003H7SH** — Pause sync while typing (completed): typing gate in `doRefresh` must be preserved.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** the root cause of `stream_closed` may be server‑side (external herdr), with no clean client‑side mitigation → the fix could be blocked or require a herdr‑side change (out of scope). **Mitigation:** diagnose first (AC4); document the finding and, if truly external, surface a blocker work item rather than weakening the client.
- **Risk:** a client‑side keepalive might not match the server's protocol and could be ignored or rejected. **Mitigation:** verify against server logs/behaviour during implementation; treat keepalive as one candidate mechanism, not a mandated design.
- **Risk:** adding resilience could change reconnect timing for agent‑status/icon updates. **Mitigation:** keep existing backoff + fail‑open semantics; icon/status paths must continue to work when the stream is down (polling fallbacks).
- **Assumption:** `pane_focused` with `focused: true` for the current pane is delivered when the pane regains keyboard focus within a visible tab (already exercised by the existing event tests); fixing stream reliability makes this the primary pane‑focus path.
- **Scope‑creep risk:** a pane‑level polling fallback, staleness indicators, or herdr‑side protocol changes are out of scope — record any such follow‑ups as linked work items, not this item's scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which focus transition is actually in scope? (A) Tab hidden→visible — already implemented; (B) pane keyboard focus within an already‑visible tab; (C) both." — Answer (producer): **A + B** — both transitions are in scope; pane‑level focus refresh (B) is the residual gap to deliver. Source: reply on WL‑0MVAS988R008PNH6.
- Q2: "Is this a defect report or a net‑new requirement?" — Answer (producer): **B — requirement** — codify "refresh on focus"; no repro attached, so this is feature/behaviour work rather than a specific bug. Source: reply on WL‑0MVAS988R008PNH6.
- Q3: "Should the work item include diagnosing/fixing the events.subscribe `stream_closed` reconnect loop?" — Answer (producer): **A — yes** — the event‑path reliability is part of this work (it underpins pane‑level refresh). Source: reply on WL‑0MVAS988R008PNH6; supporting evidence: `~/.config/herdr/herdr-server.log` (sub‑100…sub‑115, ~10 s cadence, 2026‑10‑16T07:15–07:17), `events.ts` (no keepalive).

## Related work (automated report — find_related)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MR1COW20005IO1C** – Bubble up critical items (completed)
- **WL-0MQP303A900780R0** – Escape key in Pi TUI work item detail view should navigate back to selection list (completed)
- **WL-0MOZQMNML004PB6T** – select view in next dialog does not select the item (completed)

### Repository matches
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — focus/refresh wiring for the selection list (this item's target).
- `packages/herdr/src/visibility.ts` — tab-focus visibility gate.
- `packages/herdr/src/events.ts` — pane_focused event stream (keepalive/reliability work).

Discovered-from:WL-0MVAMS4RO000H3B0

Operator report: pressing Ctrl-B then 'l' in herdr opens the Worklog selection-list pane, which then closes immediately (startup crash).

## Root cause (confirmed)

The herdr plugin imports `needsProducerReviewIcon` from `@worklog/shared/icons` (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`). During the needsProducerReview restore (F2, WL-0MVAPEZTE005T27J) the shared source gained the export, but two gitignored build/install artifacts were stale (built before the restore):

1. `packages/shared/dist/icons.js` — stale compiled shared output (no `needsProducerReviewIcon`).
2. `packages/herdr/node_modules/@worklog/shared` — the herdr plugin's `file:../../packages/shared` dependency was installed as a packaged COPY and never refreshed, so it also lacked the export.

At module load the ESM named import failed: `SyntaxError: The requested module '@worklog/shared/icons' does not provide an export named 'needsProducerReviewIcon'` → the pane process exited → herdr closed the pane.

## Fix applied (operational)

`npm install` in `packages/herdr` (refreshes the `file:` dependency) and `npm run build` in the repo root (rebuilds `packages/shared/dist`). The plugin then starts and renders correctly.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A fresh checkout/pull that changes `packages/shared` cannot leave the herdr plugin crashing on a stale vendored `@worklog/shared` or stale `packages/shared/dist` — either the plugin build step refreshes them, or the resolution is made to prefer the workspace symlink/source and fail with an actionable message rather than a silent ESM import crash.
2. `npm run build` (or the herdr plugin build) refreshes `packages/herdr/node_modules/@worklog/shared` when `packages/shared` changes, verified by a regression test or build check.
3. The selection-list pane start path surfaces a clear diagnostic (and stays open / logs) if a shared export is missing, instead of exiting silently.
4. Related documentation is updated (herdr README / build docs).
5. Full project test suite passes with the changes.

## Notes / related discovered issue

- A separate worktree-isolation gap was found during F2: worktrees resolve `@worklog/shared` through `node_modules` symlinks to the MAIN checkout's `packages/shared`, so a worktree's shared-package changes are invisible to its build/tests without a manual node_modules mirror. Tracked separately under the same discovered-from parent if needed.
- Parent epic: WL-0MVAMS4RO000H3B0.

# mode-switch-worker: identify the caller in `POST /admin/set-mode` for restart attribution

## Goal

Extend the ContextHub herdr mode-switch worker so every `POST /admin/set-mode`
it makes self-identifies, enabling the llama-proxy to attribute mode-switch
restarts (llm repo work item **LP-0MVAPNC2900145RH**).

## Context

The proxy's `/admin/set-mode` endpoint will accept optional `actor`, `source`,
and `reason` fields (llm **LP-0MVAPNC2900145RH**). The worker currently POSTs
`{"mode": "fast"|"cheap"}` only (`packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts`,
`setAdminMode`), so proxy restarts triggered by the worker are indistinguishable
from manual web-UI/API switches in the proxy logs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `setAdminMode` sends `source: "worker"`, an `actor` identifying the
      trigger (e.g. `mode-switch-worker:idle-cheap` /
      `mode-switch-worker:agent-route-fast`), and a short human-readable
      `reason` in the POST body, without changing existing failure semantics
      (409/network/timeout remain non-throwing no-op outcomes).
- [ ] Unit tests in `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.test.ts` assert the
      new fields are present in the recorded POST body for both fast and cheap
      switches.
- [ ] `docs/design/mode-switch-worker.md` documents the attribution fields.
- [ ] Build and full test suite pass with the new changes.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments and any relevant docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Additive payload only — the proxy tolerates unknown/absent fields, so the
  worker remains compatible with older proxy versions.
- Do not alter switch timing, gating, or failure handling.

## Related work

- llm **LP-0MVAPNC2900145RH** — Log the requesting actor and reason for every
  proxy mode-switch / `--restart` so restarts are always attributable
  (consumer of these fields).

## Intake Questions for Producer

**Q1 — Correct project?** This work item is in ContextHub (the worklog CLI tool). The feature describes a game screen for the Main Street business simulation game, which lives in the `tce-main-street` project. Should this work item be moved to `tce-main-street`?

**Q2 — Per-turn history tracking.** The current game state (`MainStreetState`) tracks only the *current* turn's values (coins, reputation, score, turn number) — there is no per-turn history array. The existing game-over overlay (MS-0MUWE6NCA008LDXM) shows a static snapshot at game over. To produce graphs of profit per turn, cash at end of turn, etc., the game must record a snapshot at the end of each turn during gameplay.

- (A) Add per-turn history tracking: a new array on `MainStreetState` that records coins, reputation, score, businesses count, staff count, etc. at each turn's end. **Recommended** — gives the data needed for all requested graphs.
- (B) Use only the current state's static values — show one big-number summary without historical graphs. This would not satisfy the graph requirements.

**Q3 — Chart/graph library.** The game uses Phaser 3 for rendering. Which approach for graphs?

- (A) Phaser-based line/bar charts (custom rendering via Phaser Graphics). **Recommended** — no new dependencies, fits the existing rendering pipeline.
- (B) External charting library (e.g. Chart.js) embedded in Phaser — heavier dependency but easier chart types.
- (C) Simple SVG line plots rendered as Phaser textures — middle ground.

**Q4 — Graph types.** The description lists: profit per turn, businesses count, cash at end of turn, staff count, reputation, and "any other useful stats". Beyond these, are there specific additional stats to include?

**Q5 — Summary screen placement.** "Place the cash at end of turn on the summary screen and add a link to a more detailed screen" — the summary screen is the right column of the existing two-column Game Over overlay. data.author: Map
data.comment:
**Decision (epic Q1) recorded.** Accepted answer: option (a) — treat `assignee` as a normal, non-regression-guarded merge field so `''` clears propagate cross-root. Rationale: `assignee` is a scheduling hold (assign = hold from auto-dispatch, clear = release); the status-neutral claim (epic Option A) only works if a cleared assignee propagates so the item is re-selectable everywhere. A regression-guarded assignee resurrects stale claims across roots/panes and forces `--accept-regressions` noise on every sync.

**Implementation (src/sync.ts):** removed `assignee` from both `mergeParticipatingFields` lists and added `isEmptyMeaningfulField()` so empty is never treated as an absent/default merge value for `assignee` — empty-vs-non-empty resolves last-writer-wins by `updatedAt` (deterministic tie-break at equal timestamps). `isRegressionDefault` no longer reports `''` as an assignee regression. status/stage/priority regression protection unchanged.

**Tests:** unit coverage in `tests/sync-regression-guard.test.ts` (new Q1(a) block incl. no-weakening assertion for status/stage/priority); end-to-end cross-root coverage in `tests/cli/sync-assignee-clear.test.ts` (two worklog roots, real `wl sync`, remote clear propagates without `--accept-regressions`, stale remote clear does not clobber a newer local hold, status regression still refused).

**Docs:** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` cross-root `assignee` merge rule section; parent epic Appendix Q1 updated to ACCEPTED (a) with a comment on the epic.

data.author: Map
data.comment:
Implementation decisions (Map):

1. `fetchBlockersForItem(id)` in `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` runs `wl dep list <id> --json`, parses via the shared `parseDepListBlockersOutput()`, enriches each non-terminal edge with its target `stage` via `wl show` (mirroring the hydrator's `listOutboundDeps`), and filters with the shared `isActiveBlocker()`. Fail-open: any failure yields `[]`.
2. Blockers are resolved for the SELECTED item only, cached by item ID in `runWorklistTui`, invalidated on each list refresh; the render path is non-blocking and skips synthetic `isLogDerived`/`isLogOnly` rows.
3. `formatMetadataPanel()` gained a trailing `blockedBy` parameter and appends one `Blocked By  <id> — <title>` row per active blocker (bare ID when the title is empty) after the metadata rows and before the description preview. The detail view is untouched.
4. Discovered pre-existing bug: the `m`/`M` metadata-panel scroll clamp was a no-op because `formatMetadataPanel` always returns exactly `panelRows` padded lines, so `maxScroll` was always 0. The AC requires scrolling to keep working with the extra rows, so extracted `buildMetadataPanelLines()` + `metadataPanelContentHeight()` and clamped against the UNPADDED content height. Test coverage added for this.

## Intake blocked — producer input required

The seed brief ("Whenever the selection list in herdr gets focus it should refresh the view") overlaps almost entirely with **already-completed** work. Research summary:

- **Tab-level hidden→visible refresh is implemented**: `WL-0MSBVS4AS006ZQEZ` (immediate refresh on tab regain focus) plus the `pane_focused` event path in `WL-0MSHB7DHO004RHBJ` / `WL-0MSIG3IO7009RL03`, with a tab-level `resume-poll` fallback. Code: `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (`onPaneFocused` → `doRefresh(true)`; `resume-poll` task).
- **Tab-focus visibility gating is implemented**: `WL-0MSJNJPRM009RM35` / `WL-0MSKUAT5D00443GA` (`visibility.ts` — `HERDR_TAB_ID` + `herdr tab get` → `result.tab.focused`).

So the requested capability appears to already exist. I need to know the **residual gap** before drafting a brief.

### Q1 — Which focus transition is actually in scope?

- **A.** Tab regains focus (hidden → visible) — already implemented and verified.
- **B.** The list pane regains **keyboard** focus inside an **already-visible** tab (multi-pane split: click / focus the list pane while the tab stayed focused). Today this relies on the `pane_focused` event; the `resume-poll` fallback is tab-level only, so if events are unavailable no refresh occurs.
- **C.** Both, including the reliability of the event path (see Q3).

**Recommended:** **B** — because A is already shipped; the only plausible residual gap is pane-level focus within a visible tab when the event path is not delivering.

### Q2 — Is this a defect report or a net-new requirement?

- **A.** Bug — the list was observed stale after focusing it (please attach a repro: exact key/combo or mouse action, single- vs multi-pane tab, was the tab already focused?).
- **B.** Requirement — codify "refresh on focus" (may be satisfied by the completed items above; then close/relate rather than re-implement).
- **C.** Duplicate/obsolete — close this item.

**Recommended:** **A with a repro** — since the implementation exists, a concrete repro is the only way to identify the residual gap. If no repro exists, **B** with an explicit residual-gap statement is next best.

### Q3 — Event-subscription reliability (evidence of a possible real defect)

`~/.config/herdr/herdr-server.log` shows `events.subscribe` requests completing with `outcome="stream_closed"` and reconnecting on an ~10 s cadence (`sub-100` … `sub-115` at 2026-10-16T07:15–07:17, matching `MAX_RECONNECT_DELAY_MS = 10_000` in `packages/herdr/src/events.ts`). If the events stream keeps closing, `pane_focused` events never arrive reliably and only the tab-level `resume-poll` fallback remains — which would exactly explain "the list does not refresh when I focus it".

- **A.** Yes — include diagnosing/fixing the `stream_closed` reconnect loop in this work item.
- **B.** No — that is a separate defect (I will create a child work item for it).
- **C.** Unknown/not applicable.

**Recommended:** **A** — the log evidence points at the event path as the likely root cause, and it is squarely within "refresh on focus".
